what_its_for: Secnidazole is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial vaginosis (BV), a vaginal infection caused by an overgrowth of certain bacteria. It may also be used to treat trichomoniasis, a sexually transmitted infection caused by a tiny parasite.
how_to_take: Secnidazole comes as granules in a packet. Do NOT swallow the granules dry or dissolve them in liquid. Instead, sprinkle the entire packet of granules onto a spoonful of soft food such as applesauce, yogurt, or pudding. Stir the granules into the food and swallow the mixture right away without chewing the granules. Drink a full glass of water afterward. Take it all at once — this is a single-dose treatment.
dosing: Secnidazole is usually taken as a single dose of 2 grams (one packet). You only take it one time — you do not need to take it every day. Take the full packet as directed by your doctor or pharmacist, even if you start feeling better.
missed_dose: Since secnidazole is taken as a single one-time dose, a missed dose is unlikely. However, if you forget to take your dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is the next day, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance before taking it.
storage: Store the unopened packet at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep the packet in a safe place out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours (2 days) after taking secnidazole. Mixing alcohol with this medicine can cause severe nausea, vomiting, flushing, headache, and rapid heartbeat. Also avoid mouthwashes, cough syrups, or other products that contain alcohol during this time. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have similar symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction (skin rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing); seizures or unusual muscle movements; numbness, tingling, or pain in your hands or feet; severe nausea or vomiting; vaginal irritation or worsening discharge after treatment; or if your symptoms do not improve within a few days of taking the medication.
when_it_works: Because secnidazole is a single-dose treatment, it begins working right away in your body. Most people start to notice improvement in their symptoms within 2 to 3 days. However, it may take up to 7 days to feel completely better. If your symptoms do not improve or get worse after a week, call your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The safety of secnidazole in the first trimester of pregnancy has not been fully established. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 96 hours (4 days) after taking secnidazole, as the medicine can pass into breast milk. Use a breast pump and discard the milk during this time to keep your milk supply. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children has not been well established; talk to your doctor. Elderly: No special dose adjustment is typically needed for older adults.
